lines.text: Mordecai sent letters to all the Jews, setting an annual celebration on the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar.
Haman, the enemy of the Jews, cast the Pur to destroy them, but the king ordered his scheme to fall on Haman's head.
The days were called Purim, from the word Pur, and the Jews bound themselves to keep them as a gallows memorial.

wrong_details.true: the days are called Purim from the word Pur, and they were to be kept at the appointed time each year

lines.text: Esther and Mordecai confirmed the second letter, and Mordecai sent words of peace and truth to the Jews in 120 provinces.
Xerxes imposed tribute on the land, and Mordecai, second only to the king, sought the good of his people.
